headline: Iran attacks US military base in Jordan after US destroys 5 oil tankers
summary: Tehran targets the Al-Azraq air base with missiles in retaliation for American strikes on Iranian tankers, as global oil prices climb toward $100 a barrel.
details: Iran's Revolutionary Guards launched a missile attack on the US air base of Al-Azraq in Jordan, vowing retaliation for American strikes on Iranian oil tankers.
The 'punitive operation' targeted maintenance facilities, deployment locations, and fighter jet shelters. Jordan's army reported shooting down 18 missiles during the attack.
The escalation follows a US operation that destroyed five Iranian oil tankers after Iran targeted an American warship, marking the second such clash in less than a week.
Tehran has warned that oil tankers off US-allied Kuwait and Bahrain will be targeted next, urging crews to abandon their vessels.
The conflict has led to a stalemate in the Strait of Hormuz, a vital shipping route for the world's oil and gas, which Iran has largely controlled since February.
Global oil prices have surged toward $100 a barrel due to the instability, with Brent crude rising to $99.38 and West Texas Intermediate reaching $94.51.
Additionally, Iran claims to have seized a modern US unmanned submarine drone in the Strait of Hormuz, though the US military describes it as an older, malfunctioning model.
caption:
Iran strikes a US base in Jordan after the US destroyed 5 Iranian oil tankers. Global oil prices are now surging toward $100 a barrel.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards launched a missile attack on the US air base of Al-Azraq in Jordan, vowing retaliation for American strikes on Iranian oil tankers.

The 'punitive operation' targeted maintenance facilities, deployment locations, and fighter jet shelters. Jordan's army reported shooting down 18 missiles during the attack.

The escalation follows a US operation that destroyed five Iranian oil tankers after Iran targeted an American warship, marking the second such clash in less than a week.

Tehran has warned that oil tankers off US-allied Kuwait and Bahrain will be targeted next, urging crews to abandon their vessels.

The conflict has led to a stalemate in the Strait of Hormuz, a vital shipping route for the world's oil and gas, which Iran has largely controlled since February.

Global oil prices have surged toward $100 a barrel due to the instability, with Brent crude rising to $99.38 and West Texas Intermediate reaching $94.51.

Additionally, Iran claims to have seized a modern US unmanned submarine drone in the Strait of Hormuz, though the US military describes it as an older, malfunctioning model.

headline_marked: Actress [[Azmeri Haque Badhon attacked in Italy]] during film festival visit
headline: Actress Azmeri Haque Badhon attacked in Italy during film festival visit
summary: The actress alleged she was pelted with eggs and drinks, physically assaulted, and forced to chant political slogans by individuals identifying as Awami League members.
details: Actress Azmeri Haque Badhon was physically assaulted in Italy while visiting for the premiere of her film 'The Difficult Bride' at the Venice International Film Festival.
Badhon alleged that she was pelted with water, soft drinks, and eggs, and was struck near her ear while spending time with her brother and family at a local park.
The actress claimed that the attackers identified themselves as members of the Awami League and Chhatra League, as well as 'soldiers of Bangabandhu,' forcing her to chant pro-Awami League slogans.
Badhon believes she was targeted due to her vocal support for the 2024 July uprising in Bangladesh, which ended the 15-year rule of the Awami League.
The Bangladesh government has stated that the process of taking legal action has begun in Italy following the incident.
Badhon has filed a formal complaint with the local Italian police, and the Bangladesh embassy in Italy is expected to provide necessary support to her and her family.
caption:
Pelted with eggs and drinks, forced to chant slogans—actress Azmeri Haque Badhon was assaulted in Italy.

Actress Azmeri Haque Badhon was physically assaulted in Italy while visiting for the premiere of her film 'The Difficult Bride' at the Venice International Film Festival.

Badhon alleged that she was pelted with water, soft drinks, and eggs, and was struck near her ear while spending time with her brother and family at a local park.

The actress claimed that the attackers identified themselves as members of the Awami League and Chhatra League, as well as 'soldiers of Bangabandhu,' forcing her to chant pro-Awami League slogans.

Badhon believes she was targeted due to her vocal support for the 2024 July uprising in Bangladesh, which ended the 15-year rule of the Awami League.

The Bangladesh government has stated that the process of taking legal action has begun in Italy following the incident.

Badhon has filed a formal complaint with the local Italian police, and the Bangladesh embassy in Italy is expected to provide necessary support to her and her family.
